subject: Term economics & co-terming: Clarify prepay ramps and termination refund mechanics
messages:
From: Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimbus-analytics.com
Date: 2026-04-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: Clarification on multi-year prepay refunds & co-terming

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we build our internal MA (mutual action) plan, procurement asked for a clear explanation of the economics around Redwood's multi-year prepay options. Two specific asks:

1) If we commit to a 3-year, annual prepay with ramped spend (year 1: 40%, year 2: 30%, year 3: 30%), how are refunds handled if we downscale or terminate in year 2? Any pro-rated refunds or credit mechanics?

2) We have existing SaaS contracts that co-term on calendar year ends. If we want the Redwood term to co-term with our January 1 renewal cycle after year 1, how would that impact pricing and the prepay discount schedule? Any penalties for early co-terming?

I can share a redlined RFP if that helps. Procurement would like this in writing for their comparison grid.

Best,
Elena
Head of Procurement
Nimbus Analytics

Attachments: Nimbus_RFP_Q3_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T13:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification on multi-year prepay refunds & co-terming

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. High-level answers below; I attached a short term-summary workbook with two model scenarios for your finance team to plug into (Redwood_Drafted_Term_Summary.xlsx).

1) Refunds / early termination mechanics (multi-year prepay):
- We structure multi-year prepay as an upfront credit applied against invoiced usage.
- If you early terminate or materially downscale in year 2, we calculate a remaining unused credit balance and offer either: a) pro-rated refund (for enterprise customers with an approved exception) OR b) a credit applied to other Redwood products/services.
- Standard commercial terms: refunds incur a 5% processing fee and are subject to a 90-day review window for usage reconciliation; this preserves cost recovery for reserved capacity.

2) Co-terming / alignment with your calendar-year renewals:
- You can elect to co-term after year 1. Options: 
  • Automatic co-term (preferred): Redwood will shorten or extend the second-year billed period to align to your Jan 1 cycle and re-calculate the pro-rated prepay credit. We do not charge an additional co-term penalty if the total committed dollars over the 3-year period remain unchanged.
  • Repriced co-term: If you request co-term AND reduce committed dollars, pricing/discounts may be adjusted to reflect shorter effective commitment; we model this as a step-down discount (e.g., a 3-year prepay discount curve vs a 2-year effective commitment).

3) Ramp schedule and discounting:
- We typically provide a blended discount that scales with committed ARR. For the 40/30/30 ramp you proposed, we can model a front-loaded discount to reflect your larger year-1 prepay (example in workbook).

Next steps: happy to run your exact numbers and produce an addendum clause for the contract that codifies the refund calculation and co-term mechanics. If procurement wants to avoid the 5% refund fee, we can consider waiving it for negotiated enterprise agreements with a sign-off from Sales Leadership.

I’ll loop in Jonas (sales operations) and Lauren (legal/product) to confirm operational feasibility.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_Drafted_Term_Summary.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-13T08:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Clarification on multi-year prepay refunds & co-terming

Looping in a quick ops/legal view:

Soojin — good summary. A couple of notes for negotiation posture:
- Waiving the 5% refund fee should be reserved for deals >= $250k ACV over term OR where we expect expansion signals (data/embedding-heavy workloads) within 12 months.
- For co-terming, operations can handle a single co-term adjustment (pro-rate to calendar year) without changing SKU pricing; repeated re-co-terming requests increase complexity and will require a re-evaluation of committed capacity and possibly a re-quantization of reserved GPU pool sizing.
- Recommend adding a clause that defines "material downscale" (e.g., >25% reduction in committed capacity year-over-year triggers reconciliation) to avoid ambiguous refunds.

I'll draft a short legal-safe paragraph; Lauren, can you confirm if we need to allow for credit-only refunds in standard EAs?

-Jonas
Director, Sales Ops

Subject: Re: Clarification on multi-year prepay refunds & co-terming

All —

Legal is comfortable with the approach, with these guardrails to include in the contract addendum:

1) Refund treatment: default to credit-only refunds applied against other Redwood services unless an exception is approved by Revenue Ops. If a cash refund is approved, apply a 5% administrative fee (we can consider waiving for strategic deals as Jonas noted).

2) Definition of material downscale: >25% reduction in committed spend for the upcoming 12-month period compared to the last 12 months; if triggered, Redwood will perform a reconciliation and compute remaining prepay balance pro-rata.

3) Co-term mechanism: allow a single co-term alignment during the first 12 months of the agreement; co-terming territory to shorten the remaining term is permissible but will reprice to the nearest discount band unless total committed dollars remain equal to the original 3-year schedule.

4) Add a 90-day reconciliation window after termination request to validate usage and finalize any payout/credits.

I can draft the exact clause language and drop it into the shared drive. Recommend Soojin offer Elena: (A) a clean addendum with credit-first default and (B) an option that waives the admin fee if Nimbus signs before 2026-05-07 and reaches $250k+ committed spend.

-Lauren
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-16T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification on multi-year prepay refunds & co-terming

Elena —

Thanks for the RFP. Per the internal review, please find the summarized commercial positions below (we attach the workbook we ran for your 40/30/30 ramp):

1) Refunds: default is credit applied to other Redwood services. Cash refunds available by exception; cash refunds carry a 5% administrative fee.

2) Material downscale: defined as >25% reduction in committed spend vs the prior 12 months; triggers reconciliation and pro-rata credit calculation.

3) Co-terming: we will allow a single co-term alignment within the first 12 months. If you co-term to calendar year and the total committed dollars over the original 3-year schedule remain unchanged, we will not reprice. If you request co-term AND reduce committed dollars, pricing will be adjusted to the applicable discount band (details in attached workbook).

4) Short-term incentive: if Nimbus signs the 3-year prepay by 2026-05-07 and commits >= $250k total over the term, Redwood will waive the 5% admin fee for any approved cash refund.

Next steps: I can produce a short addendum with the clause language (credit-first default, material downscale definition, co-term allowance, 90-day reconciliation) and a DocuSign link for signature. Would you like us to: A) produce a redline to your RFP, or B) send our addendum for you to attach?

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with procurement if that speeds things up.

Best,
Soojin Lee
